hero.description: I turn complex problems into elegant code. Whether it's shipping a game mechanic that feels right, or architecting a backend that scales — I build solutions that actually matter to clients.

about.label: About me
about.p1: I'm a freelance software engineer who lives at the intersection of engineering discipline and creative drive. My specialty is game programming — physics systems, real-time rendering pipelines, gameplay feel — but I thrive across the full spectrum of computer science.
about.p2: Every project starts the same way: understanding what you actually need, not just what you asked for. Then I build a solution that fits precisely, performs reliably, and ships on time.
about.p3: When I'm not freelancing, I'm usually deep in a personal game project, contributing to open-source tools, or learning more about new technologies I currently have no experience with.

wax.desc: A mobile vinyl record collection app built for collectors. Search via the Discogs API, barcode scanning, image carousel, tracklist and collection stats.
wax.longDesc: WAX is a personal mobile project built for vinyl record collectors, developed with React Native and Expo. It connects to the Discogs API to search for records, scan barcodes, browse image carousels and tracklists, and keep track of collection statistics. The goal was to build a polished, production-ready mobile app from scratch with a focus on UX and real-world data integration.
wax.h1: Discogs API integration — search millions of vinyl records, fetch album data, tracklists and cover images in real time
wax.h2: Barcode scanning — scan physical vinyl records to instantly identify and add them to the collection
wax.h3: Collection stats & image carousel — visual overview of the collection with statistics and browsable cover art

portfolio.desc: Personal freelance portfolio built with React, Vite and TailwindCSS — featuring holographic UI effects, scramble text animations, 3D card tilt, real-time i18n and a working contact form.
portfolio.role: Solo developer — design, development, SEO, deployment
portfolio.longDesc: This portfolio was built from scratch to showcase my projects and freelance services. Every visual detail was crafted intentionally — from the holographic scan effects and holo cubes, to the scramble text typing effect powered by anime.js, the 3D card tilt on hover, and the animated navbar underline. The site is fully bilingual (EN/FR) with real-time language switching via i18next, and includes a working contact form via EmailJS.
portfolio.h1: Holographic UI system — custom HoloScan, HoloCube and holo label components with Motion animations, scanlines and glow effects consistent across all sections
portfolio.h2: Scramble text typing effect — anime.js scrambleText plugin animating role titles in the hero section with configurable cursor and reveal speed
portfolio.h3: Bilingual i18n — full EN/FR translation with real-time language switching via i18next, auto-detecting browser language on first load

nexusengine.desc: Custom C++ game engine built around an ECS architecture with OpenGL 3.3+ rendering, rigid body physics, and a playable survival shooter sample demonstrating the full pipeline.
nexusengine.role: Solo developer — architecture, rendering, physics, demo game
nexusengine.longDesc: NexusEngine is a personal deep-dive into the internals of a real-time 3D engine. Rather than relying on existing frameworks, the goal was to build every layer from scratch — from the rendering pipeline to the physics simulation — to truly understand what happens under the hood of modern game engines. The project includes a playable survival shooter demo as a full validation of the engine pipeline.
nexusengine.h1: Entity-Component System (ECS) — data-oriented architecture for cache efficiency and modularity, with clean separation between entities, components and systems
nexusengine.h2: OpenGL 3.3+ renderer — custom pipeline with shader management, VAO/VBO handling, texture loading and a basic lighting model, fully decoupled from game logic
nexusengine.h3: Rigid body physics — AABB collision detection, velocity integration and collision response, implemented without any third-party physics library

daimon.desc: An independent 2D action game developed solo since 2025 in Unity/C#. Full ownership of game architecture, gameplay programming, combat mechanics and UI/UX.
daimon.role: Solo developer — architecture, gameplay, UI/UX, technical direction
daimon.longDesc: Daimon is an independent 2D action game developed solo since January 2025, after an initial prototype phase used to learn Unity's fundamentals. This is a personal creative and technical challenge: designing, building and shipping a complete game from scratch, on my own terms. Artwork and visual assets are sourced externally — everything else is handled solo.
daimon.h1: Gameplay programming — player controller, combat mechanics, enemy behaviours and interactions designed and implemented from scratch
daimon.h2: Game architecture — overall system structure, scene management, game loop and technical direction handled end to end
daimon.h3: Active development — a first playable demo was released during the early learning phase; the project has since grown significantly in scope and quality

eokko.desc: A multi-context ERP developed on Next.js. This product aims to centralize data from multiple businesses in a single platform to facilitate business management.
eokko.longDesc: Eokko is a next-generation ERP platform designed to centralize data from multiple businesses within a single unified interface. The main challenge was architecting a system capable of supporting multiple company contexts simultaneously while keeping the interface fluid and maintainable. Key modules were designed with a strong focus on UX and real-time collaboration.
eokko.h1: Real-time Kanban board — multi-user synchronized task management with WebSockets, allowing seamless collaboration across sessions without page refresh
eokko.h2: Customizable navbar — drag-and-drop reorganization, personal favorites system, and collapsible parent category grouping for each user's workflow
eokko.h3: Kubernetes deployment — scalable infrastructure with GitLab CI/CD pipeline automating builds, tests and deployments across staging and production environments

timetoplay.desc: A hypercasual mini-games hub developed on Unity, centralizing mini-games in a single platform with real rewards following competitions between players. Available on Android & iOS.
timetoplay.longDesc: TimeToPlay is a mobile platform centralizing several hypercasual mini-games within a single interface. Players compete in short, accessible game sessions and earn real rewards based on competition results. The project was delivered from concept to production on both Android and iOS stores, coordinating a 5-person development team across the full development cycle.
timetoplay.h1: Competition system — real-time and score-based competitions between players with dynamic leaderboards and real reward attribution via PlayFab
timetoplay.h2: PlayFab integration — complete backend for player accounts, scores, leaderboards and reward management in real time
timetoplay.h3: 100+ downloads in 3 months — delivered on time with a 5-person team, deployed and maintained on Android (Google Play) and iOS (App Store)

virtuallab.desc: A virtual reality game about laboratory experiences made for Meta Quest 2 & 3 on Unity. Complete quests by following the narrator's instructions through immersive lab environments.
virtuallab.role: Solo VR Developer — commissioned by EURL ECVAM (EU Commission)
virtuallab.longDesc: Virtual Lab is an educational VR experience commissioned by EURL ECVAM, the European Union's reference laboratory for alternatives to animal testing. Published for free on the Meta Quest Store, the experience targets high school students aged 14-18 and guides them through realistic laboratory experiments via a virtual professor narrator. Available in both VR (Meta Quest 2 & 3) and Desktop (Windows) versions.
virtuallab.h1: Commissioned by EURL ECVAM (EU Commission) — official pedagogical tool promoting 3Rs education (Replacement, Reduction, Refinement) and alternatives to animal testing
virtuallab.h2: Immersive lab interactions — cell culture, microscopy, automation and chemical assessment with physics-based VR interactions faithful to real laboratory gestures
virtuallab.h3: Dual platform — VR standalone version (Meta Quest 2 & 3) and Desktop version (Windows), published for free on the Meta Quest Store

archivizvr.desc: Realistic architectural visualization in virtual reality developed on Unreal Engine 5.1 for Meta Quest 2, built during an internship at Scissors In The Plug using Blueprints and 3D assets.
archivizvr.role: Game Programmer (Internship) — Scissors In The Plug
archivizvr.longDesc: ArchivizVR is a real-time architectural visualization demo in VR, developed during an internship at Scissors In The Plug, a Bordeaux-based studio specializing in immersive technologies. The main challenge was achieving a high level of visual fidelity — photorealistic materials, dynamic lighting — while meeting the strict performance constraints of Meta Quest 2 standalone hardware.
archivizvr.h1: Photoreal standalone VR — high-fidelity architectural environments with PBR materials and dynamic lighting, optimized for Meta Quest 2 without a PC
archivizvr.h2: Interactive features in Blueprints & C++ — navigation through architectural spaces, interactive points of interest and scene element manipulation
archivizvr.h3: UE5 VR optimization — Lumen adapted for standalone, Nanite disabled, draw call reduction and LOD management to maintain stable framerate on Quest hardware

findux.desc: Real-time monitoring web application built with Django and Vue.js for the metropolis of Bordeaux. Automates application integration via GitLab pipelines and assists the integration & supervision department.
findux.longDesc: FindUX is an internal web application developed for the IT integration and operations department of the Métropole de Bordeaux. Faced with a growing application portfolio and time-consuming manual deployment processes, the goal was to centralize real-time supervision and automate integration pipelines to make production releases more reliable and faster.
findux.h1: Real-time monitoring dashboard — Vue.js interface giving operations teams instant visibility over deployment states, alerts and application health indicators
findux.h2: GitLab CI/CD automation — pipelines automating build, test and deployment phases, reducing manual interventions and human error risk
findux.h3: Ansible automation scripts — Linux infrastructure automation for recurring system administration tasks, saving significant time for the operations team
